(Phoenix, Arizona) | college = [[Fresno State Bulldogs men's basketball|Fresno State]] (2013–2017) | draft_year = 2017 | career_start = 2017 | years1 = 2017 | team1 = [[BG Göttingen]] | years2 = [[2017–18 NBA G League season|2017]]–[[2018–19 NBA G League season|2019]] | team2 = [[Westchester Knicks]] | years3 = [[2019–20 NBA G League season|2019–2020]] | team3 = [[Raptors 905]] | years4 = {{nbay|2019|end}} | team4 = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | years5 = {{nbay|2019|end}}–{{nbay|2020|end}} | team5 = [[Toronto Raptors]] | years6 = [[2019–20 NBA G League season|2020]] | team6 = →Raptors 905 | years7 = {{nbay|2021|full=y}} | team7 = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | years8 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team8 = →[[Oklahoma City Blue]] | years9 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team9 = [[Austin Spurs]] | years10 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team10 = [[Valley Suns]] | years11 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team11 = [[Memphis Hustle]] | years12 = 2026–present | team12 = [[BC Roma SPQR|Roma SPQR]] | highlights = *[[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] Freshman of the Year (2014) }} '''Paul Watson Jr.''' (born December 30, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[BC Roma SPQR|Roma SPQR]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Fresno State Bulldogs men's basketball|Fresno State Bulldogs]]. ==High school career== Watson attended [[Paradise Valley High School]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona]]. He led the team to a state championship and was named Most Valuable Player.{{cite news|last1=Esparza-Cronkite|first1=Jose|title=Watson calls Suns workout 'amazing'|url=https://kdminer.com/news/2017/jun/12/watson-calls-suns-workout-amazing/|access-date=May 19, 2018|work=[[Kingman Daily Miner]]|date=June 12, 2017}} ==College career== Watson was selected as the [[Mountain West Conference]] Freshman of the Year in 2014 after averaging 10 points and 4.7 rebounds per game.{{cite web|last1=Moore|first1=Jackson|title=Watson: MW Freshman Of The Year|url=https://247sports.com/college/fresno-state/Article/Watson-MW-Freshman-Of-The-Year-105081342|website=247sports|access-date=May 19, 2018}} As a junior, he was sidelined with an ankle injury in the last three games of the regular season which limited his minutes. He helped the Bulldogs reach the NCAA Tournament for the first time since 2001 that year.{{cite news|last1=Kuwada|first1=Robert|title=Fresno State's Paul Watson embracing multi-position role on court|url=http://www.fresnobee.com/sports/college/mountain-west/fresno-state/bulldogs-basketball/article113410868.html|access-date=May 19, 2018|work=[[Fresno Bee]]|date=November 8, 2016}} Watson posted 7.7 points per game as a junior.{{cite news|title=Mountain West Conference college basketball season preview for 2016–17|url=http://sports.usatoday.com/2016/11/08/mountain-west-conference-college-basketball-season-preview-for-201617/|access-date=May 19, 2018|work=[[USA Today]]|date=November 8, 2016}} As a senior, he averaged 11.4 points, 5.2 rebound and 1.4 assists per game and made 33 starts. Watson participated in the College Basketball Slam Dunk competition in 2017. ==Professional career== ===BG Göttingen (2017)=== Prior to the [[2017 NBA draft]], Watson worked out with the [[Phoenix Suns]]. After going undrafted in the draft, Watson joined the [[Toronto Raptors]] for the Las Vegas Summer League and averaged 4 points per game in five games. Watson signed with [[BG Göttingen]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] in August 2017.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.de/news/news-bbl/goettingen-holt-paul-watson|title=Göttingen holt Paul Watson|website=Basketball.de|access-date=May 19, 2018|language=German|date=August 11, 2017|archive-date=August 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180826063605/https://basketball.de/news/news-bbl/goettingen-holt-paul-watson|url-status=dead}} However, he was released by the club in October after appearing in one game and scoring six points and grabbing two rebounds.{{cite web|last1=Fleischmann|first1=Sven|title=Göttingen trennt sich von Paul Watson|url=http://www.bblprofis.de/index.php/2017/10/17/goettingen-trennt-sich-von-paul-watson/|website=BBLprofis.de|access-date=May 19, 2018|language=German|date=October 17, 2017}} ===Westchester Knicks (2017–2019)=== Watson was selected with the fifth pick in the first round of the [[2017 NBA G League draft]] by the [[Westchester Knicks]] and signed with the team.{{cite web|title=Westchester Knicks snag Paul Watson, 5 more in 2017 NBAGL Draft|url=http://thesportsdaily.com/2017/10/22/westchester-knicks-snag-paul-watson-5-more-in-2017-nbagl-draft/|website=The Sports Daily|date=22 October 2017 |access-date=May 19, 2018}} He averaged 6.2 points and 3.4 rebounds per game in his first season with the Knicks. Watson signed a deal with the [[New York Knicks]] on October 5, 2018,{{cite news |title=Knicks' Paul Watson: Inks deal with Knicks |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/knicks-paul-watson-inks-deal-with-knicks/ |access-date=October 7, 2018 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=October 5, 2018}} but was waived two days later.{{cite news |title=Paul Watson: Waived by Knicks|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/paul-watson-waived-by-knicks/ |access-date=October 7, 2018 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=October 7, 2018}} He was added to the Westchester Knicks training camp roster.{{cite web |title=Westchester Knicks Announce 2018–19 Training Camp Roster |url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-2018-19-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 23, 2018 |date=October 23, 2018 |archive-date=July 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190720013334/https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-2018-19-training-camp-roster/ |url-status=dead }} ===Raptors 905 (2019–2020)=== For the 2019–20 season, the [[Raptors 905]] acquired Watson's returning player rights from Westchester.{{cite web |title= Raptors 905 Acquire Returning Rights To Watson |url= https://raptors905.gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-acquire-returning-rights-to-watson/ |website= NBA.com |access-date= November 17, 2019 |date= October 15, 2019 |archive-date= October 23, 2020 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201023001013/https://raptors905.gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-acquire-returning-rights-to-watson/ |url-status= dead }} He averaged 18.4 points and 7.4 rebounds per game, making 13 starts.{{cite news |title=Hawks sign Paul Watson from G League to 10-day contract |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28434281/hawks-sign-paul-watson-g-league-10-day-contract |access-date=January 6, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 6, 2020}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2020)=== On January 6, 2020, the [[Atlanta Hawks]] announced that they had signed Watson to 10-day contract.{{cite web|title=Hawks Sign Paul Watson To 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-sign-paul-watson-10-day-contract|date=January 6, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 6, 2020}} On January 15, 2020, the [[Atlanta Hawks]] announced that they had released Watson.{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Release Paul Watson Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-release-paul-watson-jr|date=January 15, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 15, 2020}} ===Toronto Raptors (2020–2021)=== Watson was signed to a two-way deal with the [[Toronto Raptors]] on January 15, 2020.{{cite web |title=Who is Paul Watson? Fast facts on the Toronto Raptors' latest signing |url=https://ca.nba.com/news/who-is-paul-watson-fast-facts-on-the-toronto-raptors-latest-signing-raptors-905/1djg1y8ffwlwu1o6eew5tii2zf |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 15, 2020 |date=January 15, 2020}} On August 14, 2020, Watson had an NBA career high 27 minutes, 22 points and six rebounds coming off the bench to lead the Raptors to a 117–109 win in their final regular season game in the [[2020 NBA Bubble|NBA Restart Season]] against the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web|title=10 things: Stanley Johnson, Paul Watson cap regular season with another win|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/10-things-stanley-johnson-and-paul-watson-cap-regular-season-with-another-win-210629418.html|access-date=2020-08-15|website=ca.sports.yahoo.com|date=14 August 2020 |language=en-CA}} On December 19, 2020, Watson got converted from a two-way contract to a multi-year contract.{{Cite web|title=Raptors convert Paul Watson Jr. to main roster contract, cut Brissett, A Johnson, and Ellenson|url=https://www.raptorsrepublic.com/2020/12/19/report-raptors-convert-paul-watson-jr-to-main-roster-contract-cut-brissett-a-johnson-and-ellenson/|access-date=2020-12-19|website=raptorsrepublic.com|date=19 December 2020 |language=en-CA}} On April 16, 2021, Watson scored a career-high with 30 points and 8 made threes, leading the Raptors to a 113–102 victory against the [[Orlando Magic]]. On August 3, he was waived by the Raptors.{{Cite web|first=Scott|last=Rafferty|title=Toronto Raptors waive DeAndre' Bembry, Rodney Hood and Paul Watson|url=https://ca.nba.com/news/toronto-raptors-waive-deandre-bembry-rodney-hood-and-paul-watson/1pbb39v7cfky91pcqskber8ug0|website=NBA.com|date=August 3, 2021|access-date=August 4, 2021}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2021–2022)=== On September 15, 2021, Watson signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], on a two-way contract with the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Paul Watson Jr. to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/release/watson-210915|website=NBA.com|date=September 15, 2021|access-date=September 15, 2021}} On December 29, 2021, Watson played a career-high 37 minutes in a 115–97 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|title=Oklahoma City Thunder at Phoenix Suns Box Score, December 29, 2021|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202112290PHO.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|date=December 29, 2021|access-date=January 13, 2022}} On February 10, 2022, Watson was released by the Thunder.{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Thunder Sign Lindy Waters III To Two-Way Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/02/thunder-sign-lindy-waters-iii-to-two-way-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=February 10, 2022|access-date=October 12, 2023}} ===Austin Spurs (2023–2024)=== On October 10, 2023, Watson signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]], but was waived two days later.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Spurs Sign, Waive Paul Watson, Erik Stevenson|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/spurs-sign-paul-watson-erik-stevenson.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 12, 2023|access-date=October 12, 2023}} On October 31, he joined the [[Austin Spurs]].{{cite web|title=Austin Spurs Announce 2023–24 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/austin-spurs-announce-2023-24-training-camp-roster/n-6027310|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 31, 2023|access-date=November 14, 2023}} ===Valley Suns (2024–2025)=== On October 16, 2024, Watson signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]], but was waived the next day.{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Gauruder|title=Suns Sign, Waive Paul Watson|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/suns-sign-paul-watson.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 17, 2023|access-date=October 19, 2024}} On October 27, he joined the [[Valley Suns]].{{cite web|title=Valley Suns Announce 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://valley.gleague.nba.com/news/valley-suns-announce-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 27,
